title: The Forgotten Hollow
premise: Quentin Vasquez has spent her life in the Hollow, a valley where magic cannot follow, carving bones that whisper to her of the dead. When a dying stranger presses a map into her hands and dies mid-sentence, Quentin learns the stranger's soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain—and so was her own mother's, decades ago. Guided by the map and an unlikely found family of exiles, she crosses into the magic-soaked lands beyond the valley, where her bone-hearing becomes both weapon and liability. At the court beneath the mountain, Quentin discovers she is herself half-soul, sold before birth, and must choose between reclaiming her stolen piece or freeing every soul the court holds. She shatters the ledger that binds them all, losing her ability to hear the dead but gaining a self that is wholly, finally hers.
about_author: Hazel Yarrow is the pen name of a former mortuary archivist who grew up in a coal-hollow town where family stories outlived the families. She writes quiet, bone-deep fantasy about people who inherit debts they never agreed to.

chapters.title: The Valley That Refuses Magic
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Quentin's POV. We meet Quentin in the Hollow, carving a memorial bone for a neighbor while the dead murmur through her hands. Establishes her isolation, her gift, and the valley's magic-dead rule. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as safety.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Treeline
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A bleeding stranger stumbles into her workshop at dusk, pursued by something that stops dead at the valley border. He presses a folded map into her hands and dies whispering her mother's name. Emotional beat: dread—the world has found her.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The stranger's corpse whispers fragments: a soul sold, a ledger beneath the mountain, a debt unpaid for thirty years. Quentin recognizes her mother's voice among them. She burns nothing, tells no one, and studies the map. Emotional beat: grief cracking open old questions.

chapters.title: The Neighbor Who Knew Too Much
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Marisol, Quentin's sharp-eyed neighbor and surrogate aunt, who saw the stranger arrive. Confrontation becomes alliance when Marisol reveals she once left the Hollow—and came back broken. Emotional beat: the first thread of found family.

chapters.title: Leaving Is a Kind of Dying
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin packs her carving tools and slips past the treeline at dawn; crossing the border, magic floods back into the world and her hearing sharpens painfully. The map's first mark points toward a river ferry. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration entwined.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Toll
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At the ferry, the toll is a memory, not coin. Quentin pays one of her mother's lullabies and meets Tam, a runaway hedge-witch stowing away from the same direction she's headed. Emotional beat: reluctant companionship.

chapters.title: Roadside Ghosts
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. On the road, Tam teaches Quentin to shield her hearing; the land is loud with unquiet dead. They shelter with a caravan of exiles led by Old Brist, who recognizes the map's seal and goes pale. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by warning.

chapters.title: Old Brist's Bargain
chapters.summary: Old Brist's POV. Flashback-tinged chapter: Brist once served the court beneath the mountain and fled with a stolen page of its ledger. He offers the page in exchange for a promise—free his daughter's soul if you can. Emotional beat: guilt seeking redemption.

chapters.title: The City of Salt and Lanterns
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The trio reaches the last city before the mountain, where soul-brokers trade openly. Quentin poses as a carver and finds a broker who dealt with the stranger days ago—and who now marks her as prey. Emotional beat: the cost of being visible.

chapters.title: Hunted Through the Night Market
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The broker's hunters corner them in the night market; Marisol, having followed, arrives swinging a lantern-charm and saves them. Escape costs Tam her shielding charm. Emotional beat: found family forged in fire.

chapters.title: The Ledger Page
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Reading Brist's stolen page by lamplight, Quentin finds two names: the stranger's—and her own, entered thirty years ago, marked 'partial.' She realizes part of her soul was sold before her birth. Emotional beat: identity upended.

chapters.title: Whose Hands Are These
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, interior and raw. Quentin spirals—was her gift hers, or the missing piece echoing? Marisol grounds her: whoever sold you, this life you built is yours. They climb toward the mountain passes. Emotional beat: choosing oneself despite doubt.

chapters.title: The Pass of Hanging Bells
chapters.summary: Old Brist's POV. The party crosses a pass strung with bells that ring for lies; each traveler must pass beneath and speak a truth. Brist confesses he sold information to the court years ago. Trust fractures and re-forms. Emotional beat: honesty as penance.

chapters.title: The Court's Herald
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A herald of the court meets them on the glacier, offering Quentin her missing soul-piece freely if she surrenders the ledger page and leaves the others. She refuses. The herald smiles: 'Then come claim it from the shelf.' Emotional beat: temptation resisted.

chapters.title: Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Descent through the court's outer halls—a vaulted dark lit by souls kept in glass. Tam nearly loses himself to their murmuring pull; Quentin anchors him by letting him hear her steady heartbeat. Emotional beat: love as lifeline.

chapters.title: The Shelf of Names
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. In the archive, Quentin finds her mother's name and the stranger's, and speaks with her mother's preserved soul-echo: her mother sold Quentin's piece to buy passage home to the Hollow. Forgiveness begins. Emotional beat: inheritance reunderstood.

chapters.title: Audience with the Under-Court
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Brought before the court's magistrates, Quentin bargains: the ledger page for every soul listed on it. The court counters—they'll return only what she carries out in her own two hands. Emotional beat: rage sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Carving That Screams
chapters.summary: Old Brist's POV. While the court deliberates, Brist sacrifices himself to trigger the vault's old flaw he built decades ago, buying Quentin access to the ledger itself. His last thought is his daughter's name. Emotional beat: sacrifice as atonement.

chapters.title: Shattering the Ledger
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Climax. Quentin carves the great ledger-bone and breaks it; souls pour free like released birds, including Brist's daughter and the stranger. The court unravels as its contracts void. Quentin's own missing piece returns—and with it, overwhelming silence. Emotional beat: triumph braided with loss.

chapters.title: Silence Where the Dead Sang
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Above ground, the survivors regroup; Quentin cannot hear the dead anymore and mourns it like a limb. Tam and Marisol refuse to let her retreat alone. The freed souls' gratitude arrives as a single carved token left at her tent. Emotional beat: grief becoming gratitude.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin returns to the Hollow with Tam and Marisol, burying the stranger's bones properly and setting Brist's token beside her mother's grave. The valley stays magicless—but Quentin no longer needs magic to feel whole. Emotional beat: peace earned, not given.

chapters.title: The Carver's New Apprentice
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Quentin's POV, one year later. Quentin teaches Tam the carving craft; a child arrives at the workshop clutching a bone that hums faintly even here. Quentin takes her in. Some inheritances are chosen. Emotional beat: found family complete, story open like a door.
